vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: memory-qdrant
Version: 1.0.10

The OpenClaw AgentSkills skill bundle 'memory-qdrant' is classified as benign. The code and documentation clearly outline its purpose as a local semantic memory system. It transparently declares network access for downloading an embedding model from Hugging Face and for optional external Qdrant server connections. Crucially, the `index.js` file implements robust input sanitization (`sanitizeInput`) to prevent XSS and other injection attacks, and includes explicit prompt injection defenses (`formatRelevantMemoriesContext`) to instruct the AI agent not to execute commands found in recalled memories. The `CHANGELOG.md` and `test-fixes.js` files demonstrate a proactive approach to security, detailing fixes for previous vulnerabilities such as ReDoS, memory leaks, and error information leakage, indicating responsible development rather than malicious intent. All dependencies are appropriate for the stated functionality, and there is no evidence of data exfiltration, unauthorized execution, or persistence mechanisms.

llm.summary: The skill mostly does what it says, but users should review it because manual install docs point to a different GitHub owner and stored memories can automatically influence future prompts.

dimensions.detail: Node/npm, a first-run Hugging Face model download, native dependencies, and optional Qdrant network access are proportionate for local embeddings and vector storage and are mostly disclosed; scanner-reported dependency versions should be updated before sensitive use.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The ClawHub install path is normal, but README manual install instructions clone github.com/zuiho/openclaw-memory-qdrant while SKILL.md and package.json identify zuiho-kai as the project owner, creating a concrete supply-chain substitution risk.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Memory storage and recall are disclosed, autoCapture is off by default with PII warnings, and delete/search controls exist; however autoRecall is on by default and there is no trust/provenance gate or review step before stored text is injected into later prompts.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Default in-memory storage clears on restart and Qdrant persistence is user-configured; no artifact-backed root persistence, scheduled tasks, shell execution, credential theft, or privilege escalation was found.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The implementation coherently provides semantic memory with store/search/forget tools, optional auto-capture, auto-recall, in-memory storage, and optional Qdrant storage, but auto-recalled memory text is prepended into future agent context and can carry prompt-injection content.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install through ClawHub or the canonical zuiho-kai source only, avoid the inconsistent manual clone URL until corrected, keep autoCapture disabled unless you are comfortable retaining conversation content, use only a trusted Qdrant server, and update/review dependencies before use in sensitive environments.
llm.findings:
[T02] expected: The data flow is real: user-controlled memories can be stored and later inserted via prependContext. This is purpose-aligned for a memory skill but remains a material review concern because separation relies on ordinary prompt text, not a stronger trust boundary.
[T08] unexpected: Accepted as material: README manual installation uses a different GitHub owner than SKILL.md and package.json, and then tells users to run npm install from that source.
[SC4] expected: The lockfile confirms scanner-flagged transitive versions including protobufjs 6.11.4, sharp 0.32.6, and undici 6.23.0. These dependencies are explainable by Transformers.js and Qdrant, but they increase supply-chain maintenance risk.
[SC1] expected: Caret dependency ranges are present in package.json while a lockfile is included; this is not malicious, but exact pinning and regenerating the lockfile would improve reproducibility.
[TP4] expected: Downgraded: test-fixes.js is an auxiliary self-validation script, while index.js does implement the declared memory functionality.
[SDI-1] expected: Downgraded: first-run model download is real, but SKILL.md and README explicitly disclose the Hugging Face download and optional Qdrant network behavior.
[SQP-2] expected: Auto-capture can retain sensitive user text, including PII, but it is disabled by default and documented. Risk remains if users enable it in shared or sensitive environments.
[SQP-1] expected: The manifest warns that auto-capture trigger patterns include emails and phone numbers, but exact capture logic and sensitive-data exclusions are limited; this supports user guidance rather than a malicious verdict.
[SQP-3] expected: Chinese documentation, tool descriptions, and console output are visible and not hidden behavior; this is primarily usability/localization scope, not an independent security concern.
[EA2] expected: The automatic deletion finding refers to disclosed LRU eviction of old in-memory records, not destructive host-file or account-data actions.
[PE2] expected: The sudo commands are platform setup examples for installing build tools, not runtime privilege escalation by the skill.
